name: two_sum
title: Two Sum
prompt: Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return `1` if there exist two distinct elements that add up to `target`, otherwise return `0`.
signature: int two_sum(int nums[], int n, int target)

examples.explanation: nums[0] + nums[1] == 9, so a valid pair exists.

predict_item.question: If array a has size 3, what happens in the loop above?
options: A: Loop reads valid elements only
B: Loop reads out-of-bounds at i=3 (Boundary Drift)
C: Loop does not execute
D: Syntax error

hints: Use two nested loops to check each unique pair (i, j) where j > i.
Be careful with loop boundaries: the outer loop runs to n - 1, and the inner loop runs to n.
Return 1 immediately once a valid pair is found; return 0 only after checking all pairs.

name: binary_search
title: Binary Search
prompt: Given a sorted array of integers `nums` and a `target` value, return the index of `target` if it exists in the array. If not found, return `-1`.
signature: int binary_search(int nums[], int n, int target)

examples.explanation: 10 does not exist in the array.

constraints: nums is sorted in strictly ascending order

predict_item.question: What is the consequence of placing `return -1;` inside the while loop?
options: A: Correctly returns -1 if not found
B: Premature Abort (D01) — aborts after only checking the first midpoint
C: Compiles with warning
D: Infinite loop

hints: Maintain search bounds: lo = 0, hi = n - 1.
In each iteration, calculate mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2.
If nums[mid] < target, advance lo to mid + 1. If nums[mid] > target, retreat hi to mid - 1.
Do NOT return -1 inside the loop on mismatch — let the loop exhaust its search range first!

name: bubble_sort
title: Bubble Sort
prompt: Sort the array of crate weights `a` in ascending order (smallest first) in place using bubble sort.

examples.explanation: 3 and 1 swap, then 3 and 2 swap, resulting in [1, 2, 3].

constraints: Sort must modify array in place

predict_item.question: What happens when swapping a[j] and a[j+1] without a temporary variable?
options: A: The two elements swap successfully
B: Cargo Overwrite (D03) — a[j] is overwritten, duplicating a[j+1] and losing the original value
C: Compiler creates a temporary variable automatically
D: Causes segmentation fault

hints: Bubble sort uses nested loops: outer loop runs n - 1 passes, inner loop compares adjacent elements.
When a[j] > a[j+1], swap them using a temporary variable: int t = a[j]; a[j] = a[j+1]; a[j+1] = t;
Remember that a single pass only floats the largest element to the end; multiple passes are required!

name: is_palindrome
title: Valid Palindrome
prompt: Determine if the null-terminated string `s` is a palindrome (reads the same forwards and backwards). Return `1` if true, otherwise `0`.
constraints: s contains lowercase English letters and is null-terminated ('\0')

predict_item.question: What does `s == rev` compare in C?
stdout: Comparing pointer addresses, not string text!
options: A: Compares the character contents of the strings
B: Signal Mismatch (D08) — compares array memory addresses, not text contents
C: Causes compile error
D: Returns string length

hints: First measure the string length: int n = 0; while (s[n] != '\0') n++;
Use two pointers: i starting at 0, j starting at n - 1.
Compare s[i] and s[j] moving toward the center (i++, j--). If any mismatch is found, return 0.

name: solve_cascade
